title: Not just hunger: hearts wanting to be sure.
subtitle: Four reasons the disciples gave
then: After 'Isa told them to be mindful of Allah, the disciples explained themselves. Ibn Kathir lists it: {reward}we need to eat from it{/reward}, we want {idea}our faith to grow stronger when we see it come down{/idea}, to know {idea}you told us the truth{/idea}, and to bear witness that it is a sign from Allah.
now: You believe, but some nights at 2am your heart is restless and you want to feel sure. That is not the end of your faith. {idea}Hearts ask to be reassured.{/idea} Feed that request with what reassures: {reward}the Quran, dhikr, and people of faith around you.{/reward}
old: If I ever want reassurance, my faith must be weak.
new: Wanting my heart to be at rest is human. Faith can grow with reassurance.
try: Tonight, when your heart is restless, read one page of Quran with its meaning before you scroll.

title: A festival for the first of us and the last.
subtitle: 'Isa's dua, ending with: You are the best provider

row.title: a festival
sub: for first and last of us

row.title: O Allah, our Lord
sub: for all generations, ending in praise

then: 'Isa turned the request into a dua: {idea}O Allah, our Lord{/idea}, send us a table to be {reward}a festival for the first and last of us, and a sign from You{/reward}. As-Suddi said the day it came down would be honoured by them and those after them; Sufyan ath-Thawri said a day of prayer. He ended: {reward}You are the best of providers.{/reward}
now: You ask Allah for the rent money, for the visa, for the scan to be clear. Try asking the way 'Isa did: begin with {idea}O Allah, our Lord{/idea}, ask for good that {reward}reaches your children and theirs{/reward}, and end by praising Him as the best provider.
old: Dua is just telling Allah what I need right now.
new: The best dua names Him, asks widely, and ends in praise.
try: Make one dua today that starts with Allahumma Rabbana and ends with: You are the best of providers.

title: I will send it. A great sign brings great responsibility.
subtitle: The answer, and the weight that came with it
then: Allah accepted 'Isa's dua: {reward}I will send it down to you.{/reward} But a clear sign leaves no excuse, so whoever denied it afterwards faced {trap}a punishment like no other of their time.{/trap} Ibn Jarir reported that when some {trap}took food secretly, saying it might not come tomorrow{/trap}, the table was lifted.
now: You prayed for the job, and it came. You begged for your mother's recovery, and she is home. Now comes the quiet part: {idea}do you live like someone whose prayer was answered?{/idea} Or do you {trap}hoard and forget{/trap}, as if it might not come again?
old: Once Allah gives me what I asked, the matter is closed.
new: An answered prayer is a trust. Gratitude and trust should grow after it.
try: Recall one prayer Allah answered for you. Do one thing today to thank Him for it.

title: It was not for me to claim what is not mine.
subtitle: 'Isa's answer on the Day of Resurrection

row.title: Allah asks
sub: did you tell people to worship you?

row.title: Glory be to You
sub: I had no right to that

then: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will ask 'Isa whether he told people to worship him and his mother. Abu Hurayrah narrated that {reward}Allah Himself will teach 'Isa his reply{/reward}: {idea}Glory be to You! It was not for me to say what I had no right to.{/idea} He adds: You know what is in my self, and I do not know what is in Yours.
now: People praise you at work, call you the one who fixes everything. Your family treats your word as final. It is easy to {trap}take a role that is not yours{/trap}. 'Isa, who raised the dead by Allah's permission, said: {idea}it was not for me.{/idea} Know where your place ends.
old: If people honour me, I can accept whatever title they give.
new: Even the greatest servant refuses any place that belongs to Allah alone.
try: When someone praises you today, quietly say alhamdulillah and give the credit back to Allah.

title: I was a witness while I was among them.
subtitle: Responsibility while present, Allah's watch after

row.title: only what You said
sub: worship Allah, my Lord and yours

then: 'Isa says he only told them {idea}worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord{/idea}, and was a witness over them only while he was with them. Ibn 'Abbas narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said that on the Day, when some of his followers are taken away for what they changed after him, {reward}he will say what the righteous servant 'Isa said.{/reward}
now: Your children will grow up and make choices you never taught. Your students will forget half of what you said. You answer for {idea}what you said and modelled while you were there{/idea}. After that, {reward}Allah is the Watcher.{/reward} Teach well now, and let go of what you cannot control.
old: If the people I raised go wrong later, it is all my fault.
new: I answer for what I taught while present. After that, Allah watches over them.
try: Teach one small good thing to a child or younger person today, clearly and kindly.

title: They are Your servants. If You forgive, You are Mighty, Wise.
subtitle: Handing people's fate back to Allah
then: 'Isa does not plead or condemn. He returns the matter to Allah: {idea}they are Your servants; if You forgive them, You are the Almighty, the All-Wise.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says all matters return to Allah, and calls this verse {reward}of tremendous value{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ will repeat it on the Day.
now: You have decided where certain people will end up: the uncle who left prayer, the friend who left the deen, the stranger online. 'Isa, a prophet, would not decide it. {idea}They are His servants.{/idea} {reward}Leave their end to Him{/reward}, and keep praying for them.
old: I can tell who will be punished and who will be forgiven.
new: People's final fate belongs to Allah. My part is to hope and to pray for them.
try: Make dua tonight for someone you had judged, using 'Isa's words: they are Your servants.

title: The Day when truthfulness finally pays.
subtitle: Allah pleased with them, and they with Him
then: After 'Isa's honest answers, Allah says: {idea}this is the Day the truthful benefit from their truthfulness.{/idea} Ibn 'Abbas said: the Day when tawhid benefits those who believed in it. Their reward: Gardens forever, and {reward}Allah pleased with them and they with Him{/reward}. Ibn Kathir calls it the success beyond which there is none greater.
now: Telling the truth about the dent in the rental car. Admitting to your manager you missed the deadline. Being honest with Allah in sujood about who you really are. In this world truth sometimes costs you. {reward}There is a Day when only truth pays.{/reward}
old: Being completely honest often just loses me things.
new: Truthfulness may cost me here, but it is the only thing that pays on that Day.
try: Tell the full truth today in one situation where you would usually soften it.

title: Everything belongs to Him, and He can do all things.
subtitle: The final line of the surah

row.title: mine
sub: my house, my career, my plans

row.title: His
sub: entrusted to me for a while

then: The surah of covenants, limits and the table from heaven closes on one fact: {idea}to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and everything in them.{/idea} Ibn Kathir: He created, owns and runs everything, with no partner. 'Abdullah bin 'Amr said Al-Ma'idah was {reward}the last surah revealed.{/reward}
now: The house keys in your pocket, the salary, the children asleep in the next room. You call them mine. {idea}They are His, lent to you for a while.{/idea} That is not a loss. It means {reward}the One who owns everything is also looking after it all, and after you.{/reward}
old: What I have built and earned is mine to keep.
new: Everything belongs to Allah and He can do anything, so I hold it lightly and trust Him.
try: Look around your room and say: all of this is Yours, Allah. Thank you for lending it.
